name: NICARAGUA
lead: Nicaragua is the biggest country in Central America. Two huge lakes and a chain of volcanoes cross it. People love poetry so much that it is called the Land of Poets.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow!

geo: Nicaragua sits between two huge lakes. A line of 19 volcanoes runs down the Pacific side. Several still puff smoke. It has a Pacific coast and a Caribbean coast.
The east is the Mosquito Coast, a rainforest with some of the heaviest rain in the Americas. Most cities and farms sit on the drier Pacific side.
animals: Lake Nicaragua has bull sharks, among the few sharks that swim in fresh water. Hundreds of sea turtles crawl onto La Flor beach together each year. This is called an arribada.
A howler monkey's call carries 5 km through the jungle. Jaguars still roam the Caribbean rainforests. The national bird, the turquoise-browed motmot, flicks its tail like a tiny pendulum clock.
culture: Rubén Darío changed Spanish writing around the world in the 1800s. His face is on the 100-córdoba note. Music and stories fill town squares every evening.
Masaya weavers make hammocks that are sold all over the world. The marimba, a big wooden xylophone, is the national instrument. Most meals have gallo pinto, rice and black beans.
history: Indigenous peoples lived here for thousands of years. Spanish conquistadors arrived in the 1520s and built Granada and León. The two cities became rivals.
Independence came in 1821. The 1900s brought revolutions and civil war. In 1979 the Sandinista revolution overthrew a dictatorship.
wows: You can sandboard down Cerro Negro volcano on black volcanic ash.
Bull sharks swim up the San Juan River from the sea into Lake Nicaragua.
Ometepe, an island in Lake Nicaragua, is made of two volcanoes.
Granada, founded in 1524, is one of the oldest European-built cities in the Americas.
Mombacho volcano is wrapped in cool cloud forest, even in the tropics.
Poet Rubén Darío started Modernismo, a movement that swept Latin America and Spain.
The 365 tiny Isletas in Lake Nicaragua formed in one eruption of Mombacho.

myths.myth: A volcano is a mountain on fire
myths.fact: Nothing burns. Hot melted rock called magma rises up and pours out as lava.
Native peoples of the Americas made them first. Sailors saw them and copied them.
